stemMd: A publisher finds that readers who finish its long online articles are more likely to subscribe than readers who leave early. It plans to increase every article’s length, expecting subscription rates to rise. Which fact most weakens the plan’s rationale?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The publisher offers both monthly and annual subscriptions.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Readers already considering a subscription are especially likely to finish long articles.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Long articles require more editing time.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Subscribers can read the publisher’s archive.

explanationMd: Prior intention may explain both completion and subscription. Increasing length does not necessarily create that intention, so the observed association may not support the intervention.

distractorRationale.a: Payment options do not isolate the effect of article length.
distractorRationale.e: A subscriber benefit does not show that longer articles cause subscription.
distractorRationale.c: This concerns costs, not the proposed causal link to subscription.
distractorRationale.d: The mere presence of photographs does not explain the association.
